ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Nico is learning to drive. He knows how to turn right but has not yet learned how to turn left. What is the smallest number of right turns he could make to travel from $\mathrm{P}$ to $\mathrm{Q}$, moving first in the direction shown?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, P is at a middle slightly right position, and there is an arrow above point P, indicating that Nico initially travels upward. Q is at the upper left. The shaded rectangles are obstacles: near the right side of Q there is an upper horizontal obstacle, and in the upper right there is also a horizontal obstacle; in the middle there is a left-side vertical obstacle, as well as two smaller obstacles to the left and right near P; below there is also a long horizontal obstacle. Reasoning: Nico can only turn right, so starting from facing upward, the directions after consecutive right turns are, in order, up, right, down, left, up. It is possible to arrive with 4 right turns: first go upward from P into the middle gap, turn right eastward through the open channel on the right side, then turn right southward and go down along the right-side channel, then turn right westward and pass from below the long obstacle below, and finally turn right northward and go up along the left-side channel to Q. Explanation that at least 4 times are needed: with 0, 1, or 2 right turns, the direction sequences are at most up, up-right, up-right-down, none of which has a final westward movement, so it is impossible to reach Q, which is northwest of P. If there are only 3 right turns, the directions must be up, right, down, left, and in the end Nico can only approach Q from east to west; but the upper obstacles in the figure prevent this 3-turn route from establishing a westward channel to the height where Q is located, especially the upper horizontal obstacle near the right side of Q blocks the route approaching Q from the east side. Therefore 3 times are not enough, while 4 times is feasible.

raw_record.question_text: Nico is learning to drive. He knows how to turn right but has not yet learned how to turn left. What is the smallest number of right turns he could make to travel from $\mathrm{P}$ to $\mathrm{Q}$, moving first in the direction shown?

method.method_draft: Inspect the diagram: P is near the center-right with an arrow showing Nico initially faces upward; Q is in the upper-left. Hatched rectangles are obstacles, including a horizontal block immediately to the right of Q, two small middle blocks around P, a lower horizontal block, and a left vertical block. Use the text rule that Nico may only make right turns. First show a feasible 4-right-turn route: go upward from P, turn right to go east through the open space, turn right to go south along the right-side corridor, turn right to go west below the lower horizontal obstacle, then turn right to go north along the left side and reach Q. Then justify minimality: with 0, 1, or 2 right turns starting upward, the endpoint cannot be northwest of P; with 3 right turns the direction sequence would be up-east-down-west, so the final approach to Q would have to be from the east along Q's horizontal level, but the top-left horizontal obstacle blocks that approach. Therefore at least 4 are needed, and the displayed route achieves 4.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中 P 在中间偏右位置，P 点上方有箭头，表示 Nico 一开始朝上行驶。Q 在左上方。阴影矩形是障碍物：Q 右侧附近有一个上方横向障碍，右上方还有一个横向障碍；中部有左侧竖向障碍，以及 P 附近左右两个较小障碍；下方还有一个长横向障碍。推理：Nico 只能右转，所以从朝上开始，连续右转后的方向依次是上、右、下、左、上。可以用 4 次右转到达：先从 P 向上进入中间空隙，右转向东穿过右侧开放通道，再右转向南沿右边通道下行，再右转向西从下方长障碍物下面通过，最后右转向北沿左侧通道上行到 Q。说明至少需要 4 次：0 次、1 次或 2 次右转时，方向序列至多是上、上右、上右下，都没有向西的最后移动，无法到达位于 P 西北方的 Q。若只有 3 次右转，方向必须是上、右、下、左，最后只能从东向西接近 Q；但图中上方障碍物阻止了这种 3 转路线建立到 Q 所在高度的西行通道，尤其 Q 右侧附近的上方横向障碍挡住了从东侧接近 Q 的路线。因此 3 次不够，而 4 次可行。
